pages.title: About the Author
pages.excerpt: A fixture author chapter for the reader theme.
pages.content:
I work on software teams that turn new technical systems into usable, durable products. The through-line is helping people understand what the machine is doing, what it needs from them, and where the work should go next.

This fixture page is intentionally not a mirror of the live site. It gives the theme stable prose, inline reader highlights, and normal Gutenberg blocks to render while the future content model evolves.

Good tools should make the next right action easier to see.

posts.title: Notes on Reader-Shaped Websites
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay about reader interfaces.
posts.content:
A reader-shaped website can borrow from books without pretending the browser is paper. The useful parts are progress, focus, return paths, and a content model that respects chapters.

The less useful part is fake pagination. Real web reading still has to handle font changes, viewport changes, zoom, assistive technology, and links that move the reader somewhere else.

posts.title: Structured Projects Beat Page Cards
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay about moving project content into a CPT.
posts.content: Project cards are easy to draw once and hard to reuse later. A project post type gives each entry a title, URL, summary, status, grouping, and body that can be queried wherever the theme needs it.

posts.title: Reader Block Kitchen Sink
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay with common writing blocks.
posts.content:
This fixture exists to make normal post-writing blocks visible in the reader. It includes headings, lists, quotes, pullquotes, details, buttons, separators, and verse.

A section heading

Inline formatting should keep the line comfortable: strong text, emphasis, inline_code_with_a_long_token_that_should_wrap_inside_the_reader_column, and a link.

  • A list item with enough words to wrap naturally inside the reading column.
  • A second item with a nested list.
    • Nested items should indent without becoming cramped.

A quote should feel like part of the essay, not like a generic browser default.

Fixture note
Expandable note

Details blocks should have enough padding and contrast to be tappable on mobile.

Example action
A short line
    an indented line
and one deliberately long verse line that should still fit the reader without forcing the whole page sideways.

posts.title: Reader Media and Embed Fixture
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay with images, gallery markup, and an embed placeholder.
posts.content: Media blocks should fit the reader column, preserve captions, and avoid horizontal scroll on small screens.

posts.title: Reader Data and Code Fixture
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay with code, tables, and long tokens.
posts.content:
Code and data often contain long unbroken tokens like https://api.example.com/v1/projects/reader-fixture/items?include=really-long-query-parameter-name, and those should not escape the reader.

const payload = {
  endpoint: 'https://api.example.com/v1/projects/reader-fixture/items?include=really-long-query-parameter-name',
  status: 'ready-for-reader-layout-testing'
};

posts.title: Reader Wide Block Fixture
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay with wide and full-width reader blocks.
posts.content:
Some post blocks need to step outside the normal prose measure while still feeling like part of the reader.

A wide cover moment

Wide blocks should breathe without shoving the page sideways.

The prose returns to the normal reader column after the wide block.

Media text

Media-text blocks should use a wider measure on desktop and stack cleanly on mobile.

Full-width reader band

A full-width group should create a deliberate band without horizontal overflow.

The chapter should continue normally after the full-width band.
